quote.text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
quote.author: Richard P. Feynman, Caltech commencement, 1974

stories.headline: The Open Flagship Is the One You Still Can't Download
stories.dek: Alibaba shipped Qwen3.8-Max as an API a week ago and promised the open weights "next week." It is now next week, and there is still no download and no licence. Meanwhile Meta — the lab that made open weights a movement — shipped a closed coding agent. The frontier's map has flipped: the "open" champion is rented, and the open champion went proprietary.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Travel Can
stories.headline: Focal Puts Its Magnesium Dome in a Wireless Can
stories.dek: The Bathys MG takes the magnesium "M" driver from Focal's wired Clear MG and builds a Bluetooth flagship around it, with an onboard DAC. The audiophile press, rarely unanimous about anything, has lined up behind it as the best-sounding wireless headphone you can buy — at a price that makes you mean it.

stories.headline: The Garden That Waters Itself
stories.dek: A terrarium is a garden sealed in glass — and the good ones run a rainstorm in miniature, watering themselves for years while you watch. Under a beginner-friendly surface sits a craft of substrate science, plant hunting and small, deliberate ecosystems. This is a hobby Singapore, of all places, is built for.

stories.headline: A Corridor Agreed, and Still No Ship
stories.dek: Iran and Oman say they have reached a deal on a "temporary route" through Hormuz. Read the small print and it is a metered lane, mostly in Iranian water, that Tehran itself calls less than a reopening — and then hangs on conditions Washington rejects. The talk moved the oil price. No hull has moved through it. The strait has been largely shut since February.

stories.headline: A Birthday Message, and a Fortnight's Wait for the Policy
stories.dek: In his National Day Message, Prime Minister Wong announced a "major review" of how the state supports families — the cost of children, infant and childcare, the load carried "throughout life's journey." It is the post-SG61 follow-through the country was told to watch. It is also, for now, an announcement of an announcement. The number attached to it waits for the Rally on the 23rd.

stories.headline: Resale Volume Rips to a 2026 High — as Prices Fall Again
stories.dek: In July, HDB resale transactions jumped nearly a quarter to the highest monthly count of the year. In the same month, resale prices fell again. Both are the direct result of one policy: on 28 July the government scrapped the 15-month wait-out for private downgraders, and the first read shows exactly what it was built to do — more bodies, softer prices. For an owner, the split is the whole story.

stories.kicker: The Kit · The Pocket Grows Up
stories.headline: Two Lenses, One Inch, One Pocket
stories.dek: DJI's Osmo Pocket 4P puts a second, 60mm portrait lens beside a one-inch main sensor with a highlight-taming trick borrowed from cinema cameras — the most complete pocket gimbal camera the line has made. It shipped worldwide on 30 July. It just isn't for sale in America yet, which for once puts a Singapore buyer ahead of the queue.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · The Billion and the Verdict
stories.headline: Spider-Man Crosses a Billion; Bridgers Files at 91
stories.dek: The summer's tentpole passed ten figures worldwide and held hard in its second frame. And on Friday, Phoebe Bridgers releases the album the critics have already scored into the nineties — which means the only number that matters, the audience's, does not exist yet.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · From Clock to Context
stories.headline: The Paediatricians Retired the Hourly Limit
stories.dek: The decade-old "two hours a day" screen rule is gone. In its place the American Academy of Pediatrics has adopted five C's — Child, Content, Calm, Crowding Out, Communication — that ask not how long a screen is on but what it displaces and how it's used. For a parent of an eleven-year-old, it is the most usable shift in the guidance in years. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Last Quiet Session
stories.headline: A Jobs Shock Reset the Path; Now the Book Waits on the Print
stories.dek: Friday's payrolls didn't miss — they went negative, and the market repriced September from a live hike to a probable hold in a single session. Everything held over the weekend at that Friday close. Tuesday's inflation print decides whether the relief was the start of something or a trap. Market explanation, not investment advice.

stories.kicker: Fitness · The Floor, Not the Target
stories.headline: 150 Minutes Is Where the Benefit Starts
stories.dek: A large accelerometer study says the famous weekly exercise minimum buys only a sliver of the heart protection people assume — and that the real gains sit far higher up the curve. Read carefully, its lesson isn't "do ten hours." It's that intensity, not volume, is the lever. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: An October Crunch at Home, a September Squeeze in Japan
stories.dek: Two big nights and a first-ever sprint collide in Singapore this October; across the region, mid-to-late September stacks the Asian Games, a game show and a sumo basho into the same fortnight. Book the flights and the hotels before the calendars do.

stories.headline: The Anxiety Economy Goes Public
stories.dek: In the world's fastest-growing major economy, the most Vedic thing in India has quietly become a venture-scale software business — young, precarious Indians paying by the minute for cosmic reassurance about jobs and marriage. Its category leader is profitable, doubling, and heading for an IPO. When the FT writes it up, it will have been running for three years.
